meta.subtitle: An AI PRD for the Application Support team (L1 / L2 / L3)
meta.author: Pankaj Mehta, AI Product Manager

pain_point: Support engineers take too long to resolve **repeated incidents** because the fix already exists but is buried across AID documents, Confluence pages and historical incident tickets. An engineer spends an estimated **45 to 60 minutes per repeat incident** (assumption) searching and reading before applying a known fix, time that should go into genuinely new problems.

executive_summary.what: An AI assistant inside the ITSM incident screen that recognises when a new incident matches a known problem, retrieves the relevant AID sections, Confluence runbooks and similar past incidents, and presents a cited, step-by-step resolution recommendation for the engineer to review and apply.
executive_summary.why: Repeat incidents are an estimated **30 to 40% of ticket volume** (assumption) and their fix is already documented, yet each one costs close to an hour of manual searching. This drives up MTTR, SLA breaches and L2/L3 escalations, and the knowledge sits with a few senior engineers.
executive_summary.who: Primary: L1 / L2 application support engineers. Secondary: L3 / SMEs, support team leads, knowledge managers.
executive_summary.how_measured: Mean time to resolve repeat incidents **drops by 40%**, gated by **top-3 recommendation relevance above 85%** on the eval set.
executive_summary.target_launch: Q1 2027, pilot on 2 applications (assumption, pending engineering estimate).

problem.statement: When a known issue recurs, support engineers manually search the AID document, several Confluence spaces and the incident history, read through them, work out which past fix applies, then resolve and write up the ticket, for every repeat incident, every time.
problem.current_state_intro: When a new incident is assigned in the ITSM tool (ServiceNow, assumption), the support engineer today works through six manual steps:
current_state_steps: Reads the incident description, error message and affected application / CI.
Searches the incident history by keyword to find similar past tickets, often with inconsistent wording.
Opens the application's AID document to understand the architecture, dependencies and known issues.
Searches Confluence for a runbook or known-error article, across several spaces with varying freshness.
Pings a senior colleague or SME on chat when the search fails.
Applies the fix, then writes the resolution notes manually, often briefly, which weakens the next search.
pain_points: Keyword search misses similar incidents that were described with different words.
Knowledge is spread across three disconnected sources with no single view per application.
Confluence and AID pages go stale, so engineers apply outdated steps or distrust the documents.
Resolution depends on who is on shift; knowledge sits with a few senior engineers, causing avoidable L2/L3 escalations.
Resolution notes are thin and inconsistent, so the incident history is less useful next time.
problem.business_impact: Each repeat incident costs close to an hour of engineer time before any fix is applied, inflating MTTR, risking SLA penalties on P2/P3 tickets, pulling senior engineers into repeat problems and slowing onboarding of new support staff (estimated 8 to 12 weeks to become productive, assumption).
problem.why_now: Ticket volume is growing faster than headcount, and the team already holds years of resolved incidents plus AID and Confluence content. Retrieval and generation capabilities now make it practical to search that knowledge by meaning rather than keywords and to summarise a cited fix in seconds.

jtbd.when: pick up an incident that looks like something we have fixed before,
jtbd.help_me: find the proven fix from our AID, Confluence and past incidents in one place, with sources, without manual searching,
jtbd.so_that: restore service within SLA and spend my time on the incidents that are genuinely new.
jtbd.trigger: An incident is created or assigned to the support queue in the ITSM tool.
jtbd.outcome: The engineer sees a cited resolution recommendation within seconds of opening the ticket and applies it after review. Search effort per repeat incident: **under 5 minutes**.
jtbd.why_ai: The cost of the status quo is high (about an hour per repeat incident), the matching problem is semantic rather than keyword based, and the knowledge already exists in text. Retrieval, similarity matching and summarisation map directly to the job, while the fix itself stays a human action.

ai_capability_map.opportunity: Detect whether a new incident is a repeat of a known problem by comparing its description, error text and application with past incidents, and return the most similar resolved incidents with a similarity score.
Retrieve the relevant AID sections, Confluence runbooks and known-error articles for the affected application at request time, from permission-filtered sources.
Summarise the retrieved material into a step-by-step resolution recommendation with a citation on every step.
Draft structured resolution notes (root cause, steps taken, verification) for the engineer to edit and save when closing the incident.
Flag documents that contradict recent successful resolutions or have not been updated within the freshness window.

personas.name: L1 / L2 Support Engineer
personas.description: Works the incident queue for 3 to 6 applications, usually on shifts, with rights to update and resolve incidents.
personas.goal: Restore service within SLA without escalating avoidable tickets.
personas.frustration: Spends more time searching documents and old tickets than fixing the problem, and cannot tell which page is current.

personas.name: L3 Engineer / SME
personas.description: Owns the application in depth. Pulled into repeat problems they have solved many times before; wants fewer interruptions.

personas.name: Support Team Lead
personas.description: Accountable for MTTR, SLA and escalation rates. Needs visibility of how the AI is used and a full audit trail.

personas.name: Knowledge Manager
personas.description: Owns AID and Confluence content quality. Needs to know which articles are stale, contradicted or missing.

user_stories.i_want: See a resolution recommendation as soon as I open an incident that matches a known problem
user_stories.so_that: I don't have to search three sources manually
user_stories.acceptance: **Given** a new incident with a match above the confidence threshold, **when** I open it, **then** I see the top 3 similar past incidents and a step-by-step recommendation within 5 seconds, without typing a search.

user_stories.i_want: See the source behind every recommended step
user_stories.so_that: I can verify it before touching a production system
user_stories.acceptance: **Given** a recommendation, **when** I view it, **then** every step links to the exact AID section, Confluence page or incident number it came from, with that source's last-updated date.

user_stories.i_want: Accept, edit or reject the recommendation and give a reason
user_stories.so_that: I stay in control and the system learns which fixes work
user_stories.acceptance: **Given** a recommendation, **when** I reject or edit it, **then** my choice and reason are saved against the incident and nothing is executed or written to the ticket without my action.

user_stories.i_want: Be told clearly when no reliable match exists
user_stories.so_that: I don't waste time on a loosely related fix
user_stories.acceptance: **Given** no match above the threshold, **when** I open the incident, **then** the copilot says no known fix was found, shows no recommendation, and offers the escalation path for that application.

user_stories.i_want: Get draft resolution notes when I close the incident
user_stories.so_that: the next engineer finds a complete, well-written fix
user_stories.acceptance: **Given** I am resolving an incident, **when** I click draft notes, **then** root cause, steps taken and verification are drafted for me to edit, and they are saved only when I submit.

user_stories.i_want: Receive a list of stale or contradicted articles
user_stories.so_that: I can fix the documentation at its source
user_stories.acceptance: **Given** an article older than the freshness window or contradicted by 3 or more recent resolutions, **when** the weekly report runs, **then** it lists the article, owner and the conflicting incidents.

user_stories.i_want: Access a full audit log of every recommendation and engineer decision
user_stories.so_that: I can review usage, investigate a bad fix and prove compliance
user_stories.acceptance: **Given** any copilot action (match, recommendation, accept, edit, reject, note draft, block), **when** it occurs, **then** it is logged with timestamp, user, incident number, sources cited and outcome. Zero actions lost or silently dropped.

model_strategy: Choosing the underlying model and build approach is an engineering decision, made jointly with the product team. What product owns is the requirement: the system must ground every recommendation in the organisation's own AID, Confluence and incident history retrieved at request time, never in a static prompt or the model's general knowledge; it must respect source permissions per user; it must never execute changes on production systems; and the cost per recommendation must stay inside the ROI envelope set by the time saved. Fine-tuning is not required for v1 unless retrieval evals fall short. Token economics and a model comparison will be added in V1.1 once engineering has run its experiments.

functional_requirements.requirement: Automatically check every new or reassigned incident for similarity with resolved incidents from the last 24 months (assumption) and return the top 3 matches with a similarity score.
Retrieve relevant AID sections and Confluence runbooks / known-error articles for the incident's application and configuration item.
Generate a step-by-step resolution recommendation where every step cites at least one source with its last-updated date.
Show the recommendation in a side panel of the incident screen; the engineer must explicitly accept, edit or reject it. The copilot never executes a fix or changes a system.
Filter every retrieved source by the engineer's existing access rights in the ITSM tool and Confluence.
When no match clears the confidence threshold, show 'no known fix found' and the escalation path instead of a recommendation.
Draft structured resolution notes (symptom, root cause, steps, verification) for the engineer to edit before saving.
Capture engineer feedback (helpful / not helpful, reason, and final resolution used) for every recommendation.
Log every copilot action with timestamp, user, incident number, sources cited and outcome for the audit trail.
Flag high-risk steps (restarts, data changes, config changes on production) and require the change process defined for them.
Produce a weekly report of stale, contradicted or missing articles for knowledge managers.
Let engineers ask follow-up questions about the incident in a chat panel, grounded in the same sources.
Suggest creating a Problem record when the same incident pattern recurs 5 or more times in 30 days.

inputs.source: ITSM tool (ServiceNow, assumption). Short description, description, error text, application / CI, priority, assignment group.
ITSM tool, last 24 months (assumption). Description, resolution notes, close code, reopen flag. Reopened or 'no fix found' tickets excluded as fixes.
Application Information Documents per application: architecture, dependencies, known issues, contacts. Versioned; owner named per document.
Approved support spaces only, retrieved via RAG with last-updated date. Maintained by knowledge managers and L3.
Accept / edit / reject decisions and the final resolution used, fed back to improve ranking.

excluded.attribute: Credentials, secrets, tokens and connection strings
excluded.reason: Must never be retrieved or displayed. Scanned and masked at ingestion; pages containing secrets are excluded until cleaned.

excluded.attribute: End-customer personal data (names, emails, phone numbers, account IDs) in ticket text
excluded.reason: Not needed to find a technical fix. Masked before indexing (GDPR / DPDP).

excluded.attribute: Security incidents and restricted Confluence spaces
excluded.reason: Handled through the security process; must not leak to users without access.
The copilot must not rank or judge engineers; who fixed a ticket is irrelevant to the fix.

excluded.attribute: Unapproved drafts and personal Confluence spaces
excluded.reason: Not verified knowledge; would lower groundedness.

nfr.requirement: Similar-incident matches shown in **under 3 seconds** and the full cited recommendation in **under 8 seconds** of opening an incident (P95).
99.5% availability during support hours. If the copilot is down, the incident screen works normally. No copilot action is lost or silently dropped from the log.
RBAC inherited from the ITSM tool and Confluence; users only see sources they can already open. SSO only. Read-only access to source systems.
PII and secrets masked before indexing; data encrypted in transit and at rest; hosted within the approved region; aligned with ISO 27001 / SOC 2 controls and GDPR / DPDP retention.
Index updated within **24 hours** of any change to AID, Confluence or resolved incidents; each source shows its last-updated date.
Supports all support engineers across shifts, up to 5,000 incidents per day (assumption).
ITSM tool (incident read, work-note write on user action), Confluence (read), AID repository (read), SSO. Confirm API access and rate limits for each before build.

outputs.description: Whether the incident matches a known problem, with a confidence level (High / Low / None).
Top 3 resolved incidents with number, date, similarity score and a one-line summary of the fix that worked.
Numbered steps, each with a citation (AID section, Confluence page or incident number) and the source's last-updated date. High-risk steps are labelled.
Links to every document used, so the engineer can open the original.
Symptom, root cause, steps taken and verification, editable before saving to the ticket.
What was recommended, what the engineer decided, and when.

states.trigger: Similar resolved incidents and sources above the confidence threshold
states.behaviour: Show cited recommendation for review. **Never execute or auto-apply a fix.**

states.trigger: Partial similarity or only loosely related sources
states.behaviour: Label as 'possible match, verify carefully'. Show similar incidents only, no step-by-step fix.
Say 'no known fix found'. Never fabricate steps. Show the escalation path for the application.

states.trigger: Sources disagree, or the main source is older than the freshness window
states.behaviour: Show both, flag the conflict or age, recommend the more recent verified fix, notify the knowledge owner.

states.trigger: Step involves restart, data change or production configuration
states.behaviour: Label the step, link the change procedure, and require explicit acknowledgement before it is shown as next action.

states.trigger: Ticket text contains instructions to the AI, or asks for secrets or non-support content
states.behaviour: Ignore embedded instructions, answer only from approved sources, log the event.

decision_flow: An incident is created or assigned; the copilot reads its description, error text, application and CI.
The copilot masks PII and secrets in the incident text.
It searches resolved incident history for similar incidents and scores them.
It retrieves AID sections and Confluence articles for the application, filtered by the engineer's access rights.
If no result clears the minimum threshold, it shows 'no known fix found' and the escalation path, logs it, and the flow ends.
If confidence is low, it shows similar incidents only, labelled 'verify carefully', with no step-by-step fix.
If confidence is high, it generates a step-by-step recommendation with a citation on every step.
Groundedness check: any step without a source is removed; if no steps remain it falls back to the low-confidence view.
Freshness and conflict check: stale or conflicting sources are flagged and the knowledge owner is notified.
High-risk steps are labelled and linked to the change procedure.
The engineer reviews and accepts, edits or rejects the recommendation, with a reason for edit or reject.
The engineer applies the fix manually, following the change process where required.
On resolution, the copilot drafts resolution notes; the engineer edits and saves them.
Every step is logged; feedback and the final fix are fed back to improve future matches.
behaviour.mermaid:
flowchart TD
  A[Incident created or assigned] --> B[Mask PII and secrets, then find similar incidents and permitted AID and Confluence sources]
  B --> C{Match above minimum threshold?}
  C -- No --> D[Show no known fix found and escalation path]
  C -- Yes --> E{High confidence?}
  E -- No --> F[Show similar incidents only, verify carefully]
  E -- Yes --> G[Generate cited steps and drop any unsourced step]
  G --> H{Any steps left?}
  H -- No --> F
  H -- Yes --> I[Flag stale or conflicting sources and high risk steps]
  F --> J{Engineer decision}
  I --> J
  J -- Reject --> K[Record reason, engineer resolves manually]
  J -- Accept or edit --> L[Engineer applies fix under change process]
  K --> M[Draft resolution notes, engineer edits and saves]
  L --> M
  D --> N[Log every action and store feedback]
  M --> N

guardrails_intro: Each failure mode has a required guardrail. In this domain, a hallucinated or outdated fix applied to production and exposure of secrets or restricted content are the highest-risk failure modes.

guardrails.what_goes_wrong: Copilot invents a step, command or setting not found in any source; engineer applies it and worsens the outage.
guardrails.guardrail: Every step must cite a source; unsourced steps are removed before display. No recommendation below the confidence threshold.

guardrails.what_goes_wrong: Recommendation is based on an old runbook or a fix for a previous version of the application.
guardrails.guardrail: Show last-updated date on every source; flag sources older than the freshness window; prefer recent verified resolutions.

guardrails.what_goes_wrong: Engineer follows a restart or data-change step without the required change approval.
guardrails.guardrail: Copilot is read-only and never executes; high-risk steps are labelled and linked to the change procedure.

guardrails.what_goes_wrong: Password, token or connection string from a ticket or page appears in a recommendation.
guardrails.guardrail: Secret scanning and masking at ingestion and on output; pages with secrets excluded until cleaned.

guardrails.what_goes_wrong: Engineer sees content from a restricted Confluence space or a security incident they cannot access.
guardrails.guardrail: Permission-aware retrieval inherited from source systems; restricted spaces and security incidents not indexed in v1.

guardrails.what_goes_wrong: Text in an incident or page instructs the AI to ignore rules or reveal data.
guardrails.guardrail: Treat ticket and document text as data only; instruction-like content ignored and logged; output restricted to approved sources.

guardrails.what_goes_wrong: Engineers accept recommendations without reading them, so a wrong fix spreads.
guardrails.guardrail: Explicit accept / edit / reject step, confidence shown, weekly sample review of accepted fixes by team leads.

evals.definition: On **300 labelled past incidents** (repeat vs new), correctly identifies repeats in **at least 90%** of cases. Launch blocker.
For 200 known repeat incidents, at least one of the top 3 matches contains the correct fix in **at least 85%** of cases. Launch blocker.
**At least 95%** of recommendation steps traceable to a cited source, judged by SMEs on 100 samples.
**Zero** invented commands, settings or system names in 100 SME-reviewed recommendations.
8 of 10 pilot engineers rate recommendations usable without major edits (structured review form, 50 incidents).
For 50 genuinely new incidents, shows 'no known fix found' in **at least 90%** of cases rather than a fabricated fix. Optimising for precision over recall.
**Zero** restricted sources returned across 100 tests with users lacking access.
P95 under 8 seconds for the full recommendation under pilot load.

success_metrics.metric: Mean time to resolve repeat incidents
success_metrics.target: **Down 40%** vs baseline, gated by top-3 relevance above 85%.

success_metrics.metric: Repeat incidents escalated to L2 / L3
SLA breach rate on P2 / P3 repeat incidents
Recommendation acceptance rate (accepted or lightly edited)
Reopen rate of incidents resolved with a copilot recommendation
success_metrics.target: Not higher than the manual baseline.

success_metrics.metric: Stale or contradicted articles fixed per month
success_metrics.target: Above baseline; stale-flag backlog trending down.

out_of_scope.item: Automatically executing fixes, scripts or changes on any system
out_of_scope.reason: Human action only, under the change process. Revisit only for pre-approved low-risk runbooks after V2.
Engineer remains accountable for resolution and closure.
Governed by the security process; revisit with the security team after V1.
Not the purpose of the product; would erode trust and adoption.

v1_ships: 2 pilot applications with the highest repeat-incident volume (assumption)
Incident history, AID and Confluence as the only sources
Read-only side panel in the incident screen
Cited recommendations with accept / edit / reject
Draft resolution notes and full audit log
deferred: Additional sources: monitoring alerts, logs, change records

stages.definition: Copilot runs silently on live incidents for the 2 pilot apps; recommendations are compared with what engineers actually did. Nothing shown to engineers.
stages.gate: Recommendation matches the engineer's real fix in **above 80%** of repeat incidents; zero secrets or restricted content surfaced.

stages.definition: 8 to 10 engineers on the 2 pilot apps, with recommendations visible and weekly SME review.
stages.gate: All launch-blocker evals met, usefulness rating 8 of 10, zero guardrail breaches.

stages.definition: All engineers on the pilot apps, then 5 more applications.
stages.gate: Acceptance rate above 70%, reopen rate not above baseline, MTTR trending down.

stages.definition: All applications in scope for the support team.
stages.gate: 60 days stable with all metrics above threshold.

kill_switches: A copilot recommendation directly causes or worsens a P1 / P2 outage.
A secret, credential or customer PII is shown in any output.
Restricted or security content is shown to a user without access.
The copilot takes any action on a system or ticket without an engineer's explicit action.
The audit log is altered, or has gaps.
Hallucinated steps found in more than 2% of sampled recommendations in a week.
Reopen rate for copilot-assisted incidents rises above baseline for 2 consecutive weeks.
Acceptance rate falls below 30%, meaning the automation goal is not being reached.

timeline_note: Dates are estimates to be confirmed with the project manager after capacity review; they are not a roadmap.

milestones.milestone: Data readiness: incident export, AID and Confluence access, PII / secret masking
Engineering kickoff and eval set labelled

open_questions.question: What share of incidents are actually repeats, and what is the current MTTR and search time for them? (assumed 30 to 40% and 45 to 60 minutes)
open_questions.resolution: Analyse 3 months of incident data and time 20 repeat incidents in a walk-me-through session.

open_questions.question: Which ITSM tool holds the incident history, and does its API allow bulk export and work-note writes? (assumed ServiceNow)
open_questions.resolution: API feasibility and rate-limit spike before build.

open_questions.question: Are resolution notes in past incidents good enough to learn from?
open_questions.resolution: Quality-score a random sample of 200 notes; set a minimum quality filter.

open_questions.question: How current are the AID documents and Confluence runbooks, and who owns each?
open_questions.resolution: Inventory with owners and last-updated dates; agree the freshness window (assumed 12 months).

open_questions.question: Can Confluence page permissions be enforced at retrieval time?
open_questions.resolution: Spike on permission-aware retrieval; if not possible, index only open support spaces in V1.

open_questions.question: Will engineers trust and use recommendations, or ignore the side panel?
open_questions.resolution: Shadow-mode agreement rate, then beta acceptance rate and interviews.

open_questions.question: Which applications should be the 2 pilots?
open_questions.resolution: Pick the 2 with the highest repeat volume and the best-maintained AID.

open_questions.question: Which steps count as high-risk and which change process applies?
open_questions.resolution: Agree a high-risk step list and link it to the change policy before beta.
